transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. Before we get started, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?

I came in because... well, I just keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up at all. 

I usually have to be up by 5:30 for work. I use this heavy-duty jobsite radio as my alarm, because regular clocks just get completely ruined by the thinset and grout dust. If you're cutting ceramic tile all day, that dust gets literally everywhere. I actually had to replace the AC blower motor in my truck twice last year just from the dust buildup. It's a Chevy, so the parts aren't too expensive, but it's still a hassle taking the dash apart. 

But yeah... lately when that alarm goes off, I just lay there in the dark. Sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family, and my crew. They're out there waiting on me to finish the floors, and I just... I don't know.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days or more where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it felt good at the time?

Energetic? No... I don't get like that. I'm pretty much always exhausted. I definitely don't need less sleep. 

Some of the guys on my crew do, though. They show up at 6 AM on barely any sleep, but they're just chugging those massive white Monster energy drinks all day. They leave the empty cans everywhere, too. Just scattered all over the subfloor. I always have to go around with a trash bag before we put the underlayment down, because if you leave even a little piece of trash, or like a stray screw under a floating floor, it'll click or crunch every time the homeowner steps on it. 

We had this one job last month... it was a huge living room, and the lady wanted the luxury vinyl planks laid on a diagonal. Do you know how much extra material you have to order for a diagonal cut? It's a nightmare for the waste factor. The angles take forever to cut right around the baseboards, and you're just wasting good planks. I was on my knees for three days straight just trying to get the corners flush. My kneepads got completely worn through on the left side. 

But... wait, what were you asking me? Oh. Feeling elated? No. No, I just feel heavy all the time. I don't really have energy for anything.
How long have you been feeling this heavy and down, and having these thoughts about not waking up—days, weeks, or longer?

It's been... gosh, it's been about a year and two months now. Yeah, it started a few months after my husband's injury. 

He was helping me unload some heavy boxes of porcelain tile from the truck bed. Porcelain is so much denser than ceramic, you know? A box of 12x24s can weigh like 60 pounds easy. Anyway, he slipped on some ice in the driveway and the whole stack came down on his leg. Shattered his tibia. He had to get an external fixator put on, with the pins going right through the skin into the bone. The hospital gave us all these special saline wipes to clean around the pin sites twice a day so they wouldn't get infected. I had to set an alarm on my phone to remember to do it, because if I didn't, he'd just lay there and watch those old Westerns on the Grit channel and forget. 

He loves those old movies, especially the ones with John Wayne. We actually went to Monument Valley on our honeymoon years ago just so he could see where they filmed The Searchers. The red dirt out there is beautiful, but it gets into everything. Kind of like the grout dust, actually. 

But yeah... a year and two months of just feeling like I'm dragging a hundred pounds of mortar around with me everywhere I go.
Before this current period started about 14 months ago, had you ever gone through a similar stretch of feeling this down, hopeless, or having thoughts like this in the past?

No... I don't think so. Before the accident, I was just... I was fine. We were working all the time, really. 

Actually, right before he got hurt, we were doing this massive commercial job downtown. It was a whole floor of an insurance company, putting in those modular carpet tiles. Have you seen those? They're usually 24 by 24 inches, and they have these little arrows printed on the back so you know which way the pile is running. If you lay one quarter-turned by accident, it catches the fluorescent light totally differently and the whole floor looks like a checkerboard when it's supposed to be seamless. 

The architect on that job was so picky. He'd come in with this little green laser pointer and point out every single seam he didn't like. We had to use this pressure-sensitive adhesive that stays tacky forever, which is good if you need to pull a square up to fix it, but it gets all over your hands and your clothes. I ruined three pairs of Carhartts on that job alone. Carhartts are getting so expensive now, too. It used to be you could get a good pair of double-front work pants for forty bucks at the supply house, but now everybody wants to wear them for fashion, so the price went way up. It's really frustrating when you actually need them for the reinforced knees, you know? 

Um... I'm sorry, my brain is just... what were we talking about? Oh, feeling down in the past. No. No, I don't remember ever feeling like this before.

Have you experienced anything like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or having thoughts or beliefs—like being certain you deserve punishment or have caused harm—that others tell you aren't true or seem out of proportion to reality?

Voices? Um... yeah. Actually, yeah, I do. 

It's usually when I'm working, or sometimes when I'm just in my kitchen at home. I'll hear this man's voice right behind me. It's so clear, like he's standing right over my shoulder. He says things like, "You missed it," or "Everyone knows." And I always whip around to look, but there's never anyone there. 

It really freaked me out the first time it happened at a job site. We were doing this custom shower pan—you know, the ones where you have to slope the dry-pack mortar exactly right towards the drain so the water doesn't pool? You have to use a laser level and check it like a hundred times. If you mess up the pre-slope, the water just sits under the tile and eventually rots out the whole subfloor. It's a huge liability. You have to put down the PVC liner, and then you have to do a flood test where you plug the drain and fill the pan with water and let it sit for 24 hours to make sure it doesn't leak. 

The inspector came out for that one, and he was this really gruff guy who looked like he hated his job. He had this little flashlight and he was shining it in every single corner. Building inspectors can be so tough sometimes, but I guess they have to be. If they miss something, it's on them. 

But... yeah, the voice. It sounds just like a real person standing there, but... nobody's there.
